scope: Seven downloaded legacy shards: four target shards and three predecessor-context shards. This is a targeted feasibility check, not a representative corpus-wide prevalence estimate.

requested_recipe.initialization: Fresh raw BT4 plus seed-0 auxiliary modules, not continuation from a current-only Hero checkpoint
requested_recipe.schedule: Preserve original example-based cosine schedule and warmup, not compress it into 554 updates
requested_recipe.wdl_targets: Hard game outcome, future states only
requested_recipe.history_scope: Current and all valid future input planes, including repetition indicators

successful_reconstruction.claim: A clean history-only reconstruction works on these two standard-game target shards; no original records were modified.

issues.impact: Cannot enable history by changing a trainer flag; current and future inputs must be rebuilt or sourced from official sequential records.

issues.evidence: Each sampled shard has exactly one header-derived game_id despite multiple ply-zero game boundaries.
issues.impact: Never join history by game_id alone. Use source identity, ordered rows, validated boundaries and move replay. This finding does not by itself establish duplicate games or split leakage.

issues.cause: All three uniquely connecting legal moves are rejected by the old absolute lc0_1858 codec; the preprocessor skips a window when action conversion raises.
issues.impact: Contiguous-row reconstruction is insufficient. Any gap recovery needs a uniquely verified legal transition or original PGN, without silently dropping retained training examples. No gap repair was applied.

issues.issue: Original corpus contains nonstandard starting positions
issues.impact: A standard-start replay rejects these games. Exact matching requires setup/Chess960-aware reconstruction and validation; filtering them changes the training population. Not evidence that the retained positions themselves are corrupt.

available_alternative.caveat: Different examples, population, splits and ordering from original Hero1. Default sequential materialization uses soft search-Q/D WDL and variable terminal horizons; a Hero recipe replica must explicitly use retained result_q/result_d and full eight-ply windows. This must not be labelled a pure history ablation.

next_gate: Choose exact original-data reconstruction versus the Hero recipe on existing standard-only sequential data. Then freeze the dataset/targets/order and bounded training specification, perform complete CPU input verification, refresh billing/reservations, and use a budget-gated launcher.
